text:
marie (design): quick flag — Errors overview heatmap rows are hard to scan; the entry action (three-dots) is easy to miss. thinking a left-aligned primary CTA (icon + short label) to improve scan and keyboard discoverability.

aaron (product): saw this in the demo. +1 to making the action more visible. prefer a short label like 'View details' so it's clear in analytics context.

sam (eng-runtime): fine technically but note we render the list with virtualization. prefer one tabbable element per row to avoid perf and focus noise.

olivia (a11y): accessibility: CTA contrast must be >=4.5:1, interactive target >=44x44px, aria-label should include error type and count, and provide a 3px visible focus outline. roving tabindex for row nav would be ideal.

marie (design): initial mock: left CTA (eye icon + 'View details'), center meta (error title, count), right time. CSS sketch: .row{display:flex;padding:8px 12px} .cta{width:36px;height:36px;margin-right:10px;border-radius:6px}

sam (eng-runtime): implement roving tabindex + arrow nav; store active index outside virtualized rows. use aria-hidden on decorative svgs and an offscreen span for SR text.

aaron (product): proposal: A/B left-CTA vs current right-explicit CTA on staging for 2 weeks; track drilldown CTR, keyboard-nav usage, and SR feedback. if left wins, ship.

marie (design): I'll upload comps for both variants and add acceptance checklist (contrast checks, keyboard nav walkthrough, screen reader sample strings).

dev-bot: design doc generated: https://go/redwood/design/error-heatmap-entry-cta (added to #design).

aaron (product): if no objections i'll mark design-accepted and queue for engineering sprint after current work.

marie (design): :thumbsup: I'll attach final assets and microcopy. thanks everyone.
